title: Multiplication-tower vanishing detected by localized-module Hom
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f\in A$, and $K\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A_f=A[1/f]$ denote the localization of $A$ at $\{1,f,f^2,\ldots\}$, whose elements are fractions $a/f^n$, with $a/f^n=b/f^m$ if and only if $f^r(f^ma-f^nb)=0$ for some $r\geq0$. Regard $A_f$ as an $A$-module complex in degree zero. For any derived limit $T(K,f)$ [def-weil-derived-limit] of the tower with every term $K$ and every transition multiplication by $f$, the following are equivalent: $T(K,f)$ is zero; and $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(A_f[0][q],K)=0$ for every integer $q$. Here a Hom group being zero means that every morphism in it is the zero morphism. No boundedness or nonzerodivisor hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use the site with exactly one object $*$, its identity as the only arrow, and only the maximal sieve covering. Put $\mathcal O(*)=A$. This is a small ringed site, and every presheaf is a sheaf: the sole covering-family gluing condition is the identity condition. Evaluation at $*$ therefore identifies its module-sheaf category with $A$-modules, with inverse sending a module to the one-value sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The slice at $*$ is the very same site. These mutually inverse descriptions identify complexes, differentials, cohomology, homotopies, localization at quasi-isomorphisms and hence $D(\mathcal O)$ with $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The localized sheaf $\mathcal O[1/f]$ is exactly $A_f$: sectionwise localization has one value and no sheafification change. Products and their projections are identified as well, so the Roos triangle of [def-weil-derived-limit] is the same triangle in both descriptions.

proof.text: Choose a complex representing $K$. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on this small site to obtain a K-injective complex $I^\bullet$ representing $K$ (in fact with injective terms). Put $C^n=\operatorname{Hom}_A(A_f,I^n)$ and $d_C(h)=d_I\circ h$. By [def-pur-hom-complex] this is precisely the Hom complex from $A_f[0]$ to $I^\bullet$, since the only nonzero source term is in degree zero. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], on the one-object site $QC$ represents $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O[1/f],K)$; internal Hom here is ordinary module Hom, since the only slice is the site itself.

proof.text: Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], morphisms $A_f[0][q]\to K$ are the homotopy classes of chain maps $A_f[0][q]\to I^\bullet$. The source has only its degree $-q$ term $A_f$, with zero differential [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Such a chain map is exactly an $A$-linear $h:A_f\to I^{-q}$ satisfying $d_Ih=0$. Two such maps differ by a chain homotopy exactly when their difference is $d_I t$ for an $A$-linear $t:A_f\to I^{-q-1}$ (the source-differential term in the homotopy equation is zero). Thus these classes are $\ker(d_C^{-q})/\operatorname{im}(d_C^{-q-1})=H^{-q}(C)$. In particular every derived morphism is zero if and only if this cohomology module is zero. The sign of $q$ imposes no restriction, since $q$ ranges over all integers.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-hom-tower-criterion] with this small ringed site, $U=*$, global section $f$, and $K$. The site and slice identifications in step 1 make its assertion $QC=0$ if and only if the given $T(K,f)=0$; it applies to any derived limit, without a canonical choice. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $QC=0$ implies all its cohomology objects vanish, since cohomology factors through localization. Conversely, if every $H^n(C)$ vanishes, the map $C\to0$ is a quasi-isomorphism and therefore becomes an isomorphism $QC\simeq0$. Step 3 identifies precisely this cohomology vanishing with the vanishing of all the Hom groups in the statement. Combining both directions proves the equivalence for arbitrary unbounded $K$ and arbitrary $f$, including zero divisors.
